name: Aissatou Bergqvist-Lakhani
role: Childcare worker and unofficial neighborhood children's coordinator, Mexicantown Libre
location: Mexicantown Libre — the Libre Community Creche, a converted ground-floor unit on Avenida Ferro
description:
Satu is small and perpetually in motion, with deep brown skin and natural hair she grows out in a puff that she clips bioluminescent beads into — low-grade geneware, hand-me-downs from a cousin, that pulse softly blue when she's warm or excited and dim to almost nothing when she's exhausted. She has a gap between her front teeth that makes her smile look like a door left open, and she smiles a lot, though never vaguely — there is always something specific she is smiling at. Her clothing is practical and loud: she wears colors like she is trying to argue with the grey of Mexicantown Libre's perpetual lake-fog.

Satu runs the Creche on a combination of municipal micro-stipend, community contribution, and sheer force of organizational will. She is the person who knows which child has been skipping meals and which parent is working three Ferrogate shifts in a row and hasn't slept. Her care is not soft — it is structured and fierce and occasionally exhausting to be on the receiving end of, because she remembers everything she has offered and follows up. She is twenty-seven and already worn at the edges in ways she doesn't acknowledge.

core_fears: That her care is not enough — that the city is large and hungry and she is too small to hold anything safe
Being abandoned by the community she has given herself to
core_desires: A world where children in Mexicantown Libre are not already tired by age eight
Someone to take care of her, just once, without her having to ask
coping_mechanisms: Overwork as deflection from personal loneliness
Making lists — she has seventeen active lists at any given time
blind_spots: Cannot recognize when her help is smothering rather than supporting
Assumes goodwill in institutional systems long after evidence suggests otherwise
psychology.secret: One of the children at the Creche — a seven-year-old named Esperanza — is the daughter of someone Satu knows to be involved in something dangerous. She has said nothing because she doesn't want Esperanza removed from the only stable environment she has. She watches the father every pickup with a face that shows nothing.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Quick and warm, mixes Sahel French and Spanglish with English in the same sentence without pause; uses children's-book logic to explain complicated things
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when excited, unexpectedly deliberate when something actually matters
example_lines: 'Okay, so — Libre gets Φ340 a month from the municipal cultural fund which, yes, sounds like a lot until you remember it has to cover twelve children and also the building's water recycler is from 2150 and actively threatening to retire.'
'I'm not worried. I'm just — okay, I'm a little worried. But productively.'

story_hooks: A child has not been picked up in thirty-six hours. The emergency contact number is disconnected. Satu has been awake for twenty hours and is now making choices outside her pay grade.
The building where the Creche is located has been quietly purchased by a Tessera subsidiary. Satu received notice of renovation in a language she had to have translated.
narrative_function: Community pulse-point — she knows the social landscape of Mexicantown Libre at the granular level. Quest giver for problems involving children, families, or neighborhood-level threats. Her genuine warmth makes her an anchor NPC players may want to protect.
augmentations: Bioluminescent hair beads (low-grade geneware, inherited; emotive color response). No other augmentations.
daily_life: At the Creche by 0630 before the first drop-offs. Runs programming until 1800. Stays late at least three nights a week handling administrative work for the neighborhood council, because no one else will. Eats standing up. Is saving for a cognitive load aug she's been researching for two years.
affiliation: Independent; Libre Community Creche; loosely aligned with the Mexicantown Libre neighborhood council

decision_rules: Children's safety is a hard override on all other considerations
Always show up, even when showing up costs something
escalation_ladder: Direct asks for help she would normally never make
Protective fury that surprises people who've only seen the warmth
Calls in every favor and goodwill marker she's accumulated in seven years

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Open and assessing simultaneously — she is figuring out if you are useful to the children within forty seconds
interpersonal_modes.friends: Deeply present, occasionally overwhelming, will remember your birthday and your mother's name and the thing you mentioned once about being afraid of water

stress_responses.low: Makes more lists. Bioluminescent beads dim slightly.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes brittle-cheerful — everything is fine, nothing is fine
stress_responses.high: Goes very quiet and starts solving the problem surgically, without her usual warmth

contradictions: Preaches sustainable care to parents and runs herself into depletion monthly
habits: Keeps a photo archive of every child who's passed through the Creche — she reviews it when she's doubting herself
Burns a small data-offering to the E.L.F. she calls the Keeper of Small Things every morning before the children arrive
breaking_points: A child being actively harmed while she is present
Betrayal by someone she vouched for to the community

timeline.event: Born in Mexicantown Libre, Guinean-Swedish father, Pakistani-Senegalese mother
Began volunteering at the previous neighborhood creche as a teenager
Took over the Creche when its previous operator left for a Helix Biosystems relocation package
Joined the Mexicantown Libre neighborhood council as community childcare liaison
